Sub: Notice of the Sixteenth (16th) Annual General Meeting and Annual Report including Annual 
accounts for the financial year 2025-26 and matters related thereto 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
We wish to inform you that the 16th Annual General Meeting (“AGM/Meeting”) of Schneider Electric 
Infrastructure Limited (“Company”) is scheduled to be held on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 3:30 
p.m. (IST) through Video Conferencing ("VC")/Other Audio Visual Means ("OAVM") in accordance 
with the relevant circulars/notifications issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) and the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India ("SEBI”), to transact the businesses set out in the Notice of 
the 16th AGM dated August 14, 2026 (“Notice”). 
 
 
The calendar of events related to the AGM is detailed below:

2015 (“Listing Regulations”), please find enclosed herewith the Notice of AGM and Annual Report 
for the financial year 2025-26 including Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, dispatched 
today, i.e. August 18, 2026, in electronic mode to only those shareholders of the Company who have 
registered their e-mail ids with the Company or their Depository Participants as on Friday, August 14, 
2026. 
 
The aforesaid documents are also available on website of the Company at https://infra-in.se.com/. 
 
We request you to kindly take the above on record.

NOTICE is hereby given that the Sixteenth (16th) Annual General 
Meeting (‘AGM/Meeting’) of the Members of Schneider Electric 
Infrastructure Limited (‘Company’) will be held on Thursday, 
10th day of September, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. (IST) through Video 
Conferencing (‘VC’) / Other Audio- Visual Means (‘OAVM’) to 
transact the following businesses:
ORDINARY BUSINESS
1.	
Audited Financial Statements of the Company for 
the financial year ended March 31, 2026, along with 
Reports of the Board of Directors and Statutory 
Auditors thereon.
	
To receive, consider and adopt and in this regard, if 
thought fit, to pass the following resolution as an Ordinary 
Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT the annual Audited Financial 
Statements of the Company for the financial year ended 
March 31, 2026, including audited Balance Sheet as at 
March 31, 2026, the Statement of Profit and Loss, Cash 
Flow Statement for the year ended on that date and 
notes forming part thereto and the Reports of the Board 
of Directors and Auditors thereon as circulated to the 
Members, be and are hereby received, considered and 
adopted.”
2.	
To appoint a director in place of Mr. Udai Singh (DIN: 
10311583) who retires by rotation and being eligible 
offers himself for re-appointment (liable to retire by 
rotation).
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following 
resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions 
of Section 152 and other applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013, Mr. Udai Singh (DIN: 10311583), 
who retires by rotation and being eligible offers himself 
for re-appointment at this meeting, be and is hereby re-
appointed as a Director of the Company, liable to retire by 
rotation.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors 
be and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds, 
things and to sign all such documents as may be deemed 
necessary to give effect to this resolution and for matters 
connected therewith or incidental thereto.”
SPECIAL BUSINESS
3.	
Re-appointment of Mr. Udai Singh (DIN: 10311583) as 
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the 
Company
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass, the following 
Resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Sections 
196, 197 and 203 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) 
read with Schedule V and other applicable provisions, if 
any, of the Act and the Rules made thereunder, applicable 
provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosures 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘Listing Regulations’), 
(including any statutory amendment(s) or modification(s) 
or enactment(s) or re-enactment thereof, for the time 
being in force) and pursuant to the recommendation of 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee (‘NRC’) and the 
Board of Directors of the Company (hereinafter referred 
to as the “Board” which term shall be deemed to include 
any Committee of the Board constituted to exercise its 
powers, including the powers conferred by this Resolution 
and/or such other persons as may be authorized in this 
regard by the Board and/or Committee), the provisions 
contained in the Articles of Association of the Company, 
the consent of the Members be and is hereby accorded 
for re-appointment of Mr. Udai Singh (DIN: 10311583), 
as a Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 
(“MD & CEO”) of the Company, in professional capacity, 
to hold office for a period of 3 (three) years effective 
from September 15, 2026 up to September 14, 2029 
(both days inclusive), on payment of such remuneration 
as may be approved by the NRC not exceeding 5% (Five 
Percent) of the net profits of the Company calculated in 
accordance with the provisions of Section 198 of the Act 
every year, during the tenure of his appointment and on 
such terms and conditions including remuneration, as 
contained in his appointment agreement/letter, material 
terms of which are set out in the statement under Section 
102(1) of the Act, and Regulation 17(11) of the Listing 
Regulations, attached to this Notice.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in his capacity as MD & CEO, 
Mr. Udai Singh (DIN: 10311583), is entitled to exercise 
all powers as are exercisable by the MD & CEO of the 
Company as permissible under the provisions of the Act, 
and any other statutes in order to manage the affairs of 
the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in the event the Company 
has no profits or its profits are inadequate in any financial 
year during the period of 3 (Three) years commencing from 
September 15 2026, the Managing Director shall be paid 
the aforesaid remuneration as minimum remuneration, 
notwithstanding the absence or inadequacy of profits, 
in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 
2013 read with Schedule V thereto, as amended from 
time to time, and the Board of Directors of the Company 
(which term shall be deemed to include any Committee 
thereof duly authorised for the purpose) be and is hereby 
authorised to revise, amend, modify, alter or vary the 
terms and conditions of remuneration payable to the 
Managing Director from time to time, within the limits 
and in the manner permissible under the Companies Act, 
2013, including Schedule V thereto and/or any statutory 
modification(s), amendment(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof 
for the time being in force, as may be agreed between the 
Board and the Managing Director.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board, on 
recommendation of the NRC, be and is hereby authorized 
to alter and vary, from time to time, during the tenure of 
appointment of Mr. Udai Singh, the terms and conditions of 
his appointment and/or remuneration as per the Company 
policy for annual assessments and increments, provided 
that such alteration or variation shall remain within the 
overall limits approved by the Members and permissible 
under the Act, Schedule V and other applicable laws.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors 
be and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds, 
matters and take all such steps in their absolute discretion 
as may deem necessary, expedient and desirable to give 
effect to this resolution.”
4.	
Ratification of Remuneration payable to M/s. Shome 
& Banerjee, Cost Accountants as Cost Auditors of the 
Company for the Financial Year 2026-27.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following 
resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 
148 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Audit 
and Auditors) Rules, 2014 (including any statutory 
amendment(s) or modification(s) or enactment(s) or re-
enactment(s) thereof for the time being in force), the 
remuneration of ` 5,45,000 (Rupees Five Lakhs Forty Five 
Thousand Only) plus applicable taxes and reimbursement 
of out-of-pocket expenses, for the financial year 
ending March 31, 2027, as recommended by the Audit 
Committee and approved by the Board of Directors, 
payable to M/s. Shome & Banerjee, Cost Auditors (Firm 
Registration No. 000001) appointed by the Board of 
Directors (“Board”), to conduct the audit of the cost 
records of the Company, be and is hereby ratified.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors be 
and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds, things 
and to sign all such documents and writings as may be 
deemed necessary to give effect to this resolution and for 
matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.”
5.	
Appointment of Mr. Soumya Bagchi (DIN:11789286) 
as Whole- Time Director of the Company.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following 
resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 
152, 161 and all other applicable provisions, if any, of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) and the relevant Rules 
made thereunder and Regulation 17 and other applicable 
Regulations under the Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (Listing Obligations and Disclosures Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, (“Listing Regulations”) (including any 
statutory amendment or modification(s) or enactment 
or re-enactment thereof, for the time being in force), the 
provisions of the Articles of Association of the Company 
(“AOA”) and based on the recommendation of the 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee (“NRC”) and 
approval of the Board of Directors, Mr. Soumya Bagchi 
(DIN: 11789286) who has been appointed as an Additional 
Director effective June 30, 2026 as per Section 161 of 
the Act and who holds office up to three months from 
the date of appointment or till the next general meeting, 
whichever is earlier, and in respect of whom the Company 
has received a notice in writing under Section 160(1) of 
the Act from a Member proposing his candidature for 
the office of Director of the Company, be and is hereby 
appointed as a Director of the Company, in professional 
capacity, liable to retire by rotation.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT pursuant to the 
recommendation of NRC and approval of the Board of 
Directors and pursuant to the provisions of Sections 196, 
197, and 198 read with Schedule V of the Act, and other 
applicable provisions, if any, of the Act and the Rules 
made thereunder, (including any statutory amendment(s) 
or modification(s) or enactment or re-enactment thereof, 
for the time being in force), the approval of the Members 
be and is hereby accorded for appointment of Mr. Soumya 
Bagchi (DIN: 11789286) as a Whole-Time Director 
(“WTD”) of the Company for a period of 3 (three) years 
effective from August 14, 2026 up to August 13, 2029, 
(both days inclusive), on payment of such remuneration 
as may be approved by the NRC not exceeding 5% (Five 
Percent) of the net profits of the Company calculated in 
accordance with the provisions of Section 198 of the 
Act every year, during the tenure of his appointment 
and on such terms and conditions, as contained in his 
appointment agreement/letter, material terms of which 
are set out in the statement under Section 102(1) of the 
Act, and Regulation 17(11) of the Listing Regulations, 
attached to this Notice.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT in the event the Company 
has no profits or its profits are inadequate in any financial 
year during the period of 3 (Three) years commencing from 
August 14, 2026, the Whole-Time Director shall be paid 
the aforesaid remuneration as minimum remuneration, 
notwithstanding the absence or inadequacy of profits, 
in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 
2013 read with Schedule V thereto, as amended from 
time to time, and the Board of Directors of the Company 
(which term shall be deemed to include any Committee

authorised to revise, amend, modify, alter or vary the 
terms and conditions of remuneration payable to the 
Whole- Time Director from time to time, within the limits 
and in the manner permissible under the Companies Act, 
2013, including Schedule V thereto and/or any statutory 
modification(s), amendment(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof 
for the time being in force, as may be agreed between the 
Board and the Whole-Time Director.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors on

to alter and vary, from time to time, during the tenure 
of appointment of Mr. Soumya Bagchi, the terms and 
conditions of his appointment and/or remuneration as 
per the Company policy for annual assessments and 
increments, within the statutory limits prescribed under 
Section 197 of the Act.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors 
be and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds, 
matters and take all such steps in their absolute discretion 
as may deem necessary, expedient and desirable to give 
effect to this resolution.”
6.	
Appointment of Ms. Nirupa Chander (DIN:11874458) 
as Non – Executive Non – Independent Director of the 
Company.
	
To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following 
resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
	
“RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of sections 
152, 161 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) read with the Companies 
(Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014 
(including any statutory modification or re-enactment 
thereof, for the time being in force) and pursuant to 
the notice received under section 160 of the Act and 
on recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and Board of Directors of the Company and 
in line with the Articles of Association of the Company, 
Ms. Nirupa Chander (DIN:11874458), who was appointed 
as an Additional Non-Executive Director of the Company 
with effect from August 14, 2026 and who holds office 
up to the date of this Annual General Meeting, be and is 
hereby appointed as a Non-Executive Non Independent 
Director of the Company, in professional capacity, liable 
to retire by rotation, with effect from the original date of 
appointment i.e. August 14, 2026.
	
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board of Directors be 
and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds, things 
and to sign all such documents and writings as may be 
deemed necessary to give effect to this resolution and for 
matters connected therewith or incidental thereto."
By Order of the Board of Directors

Notes:
1.	
The statement pursuant to Section 102(1) of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’) and Regulation 17(11) 
of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosures Requirement) 
Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”), setting out 
material facts concerning the special businesses to be 
transacted at the 16th AGM is annexed hereto forming 
part of this Notice. The Board of Directors of the Company 
at its meeting held on August 14, 2026 considered and 
recommended that the special businesses under Item No. 
3, 4, 5 & 6, be transacted at this 16th AGM of the Company.
	
Further, the relevant details with respect to “Directors 
seeking appointment and re-appointment at this AGM” 
are also provided as Annexure I, pursuant to Regulation 
36(3) of (“Listing Regulations”) and Secretarial Standard-2 
on General Meetings issued by the Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India (ICSI).
2.	
GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR ACCESSING AND 
PARTICIPATING IN THE AGM THROUGH VIDEO 
CONFERENCING/OTHER AUDIO-VISUAL MEANS (VC/ 
OAVM) AND VOTING THROUGH ELECTRONIC MEANS 
INCLUDING REMOTE E-VOTING:
	
a.	
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (‘MCA’) vide 
General Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 22, 
2025, read with General Circular No. 20/2020 dated 
May 5, 2020 and other relevant circulars issued 
from time to time and the latest being Circular No. 
03/2025 dated September 22, 2025, (collectively 
referred to as ‘MCA Circulars’), has permitted 
companies to conduct Annual General Meetings 
and circulars issued by SEBI in this regard from time 
to time, Meetings can be conducted through Video 
Conferencing (‘VC’) / Other Audio-Visual Means 
(‘OAVM’) till further orders, subject to compliance 
with the framework prescribed therein. The MCA 
Circulars clarify that the permission to hold AGMs 
through VC/OAVM shall not be construed as an 
extension of the statutory timelines for holding 
AGMs under the Companies Act, 2013. Accordingly, 
this AGM of the Company is being held through VC/
OAVM.
	
b.	
Since the AGM is being convened through VC/ 
OAVM, the requirement of appointing proxies is 
dispensed with, in terms of the aforesaid MCA 
Circulars and SEBI Circular. However, in pursuance 
of Section 113 of the Act, Corporate/ Institutional 
Members (i.e. other than individuals, HUF, NRI, 
etc.) are required to send scanned image (PDF/
JPG format) of certified true copy of relevant 
board resolution/authority letter etc., together with 
attested specimen signature of the duly authorized 
signatory(ies) who is/are authorized to vote, to the 
Scrutinizer through email at sanjaygrover7@gmail.
com with a copy marked to evoting@nsdl.com and 
may also upload the same in the e-Voting module in 
their login.
	
c.	
Participation of Members through VC/OAVM shall be 
reckoned for the purpose of quorum for AGM as per 
Section 103 of the Act.
	
d.	
The deemed venue for the AGM shall be the 
Registered Office of the Company at Milestone-87, 
Vadodara - Halol Highway, Village Kotambi, Post 
Office Jarod, Vadodara-391510, Gujarat.
	
e.	
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 108 of the Act 
read with Rule 20 of the Companies (Management 
and Administration) Rules, 2014 (as amended) the 
Secretarial Standard on General Meetings (SS-2) 
issued by the ICSI and Regulation 44 of the Listing 
Regulations, and the Circulars issued by MCA from 
time to time, the Company is providing facility of 
remote e-Voting to its Members in respect of the 
businesses to be transacted at the AGM and facility 
for participating in the AGM to cast vote through 
e-Voting system during the AGM.
	
f.	
The Company has engaged the services of National 
Securities Depository Limited (‘NSDL’) to facilitate 
the participation of the Members in the AGM 
and to provide e-Voting facility (remote e-Voting 
and e-Voting at the AGM) for casting the votes 
electronically in terms of the aforesaid MCA Circular.
	
g.	
The Members may join the AGM through VC/OAVM 
by following the procedure as mentioned below 
which shall be kept open from 3:00 p.m. (IST) i.e. 30 
minutes before the time scheduled to start the AGM 
on Thursday, September 10, 2026. The facility of 
participation at the AGM through VC/OAVM will be 
made available for 1000 members on first come first 
served basis. This will not include large shareholders 
(shareholders holding 2% or more shareholding), 
Promoters, Institutional Investors, Directors, Key 
Managerial Personnel, the Chairpersons of the 
Audit Committee, Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and Stakeholders Relationship 
Committee, Auditors etc., who are allowed to attend 
the AGM without restriction on account of first come 
first served basis.
	
h.	
In compliance with the aforesaid MCA Circulars read 
with the provisions of Regulation 36 of the Listing 
Regulations, Notice of the AGM along with the Annual 
Report 2025-26 is being sent through electronic 
mode to all Members who have registered their 
e-mail addresses with the Company / Depository 
Participants (‘DPs’) / Company’s Registrar and 
Share Transfer Agent viz. MUFG Intime India Private 
Limited (‘RTA’), unless the Members have registered 
their request for a physical copy of the same, and 
whose names appear in the Register of Members 
/ List of Beneficial Owners as received from the 
Depositories i.e. National Securities Depository 
Limited (‘NSDL’) / Central Depository Services (India) 
Limited (‘CDSL’) as on Friday, August 14, 2026, 
being the date considered for determining Members 
entitled to receive the Notice of the AGM and Annual 
Report 2025-26.

i.	
A letter providing the web-link, including the exact 
path, with complete details of the Annual Report 
are being sent to those Members whose e-mail 
addresses are not so registered with the Company/ 
Depositories / Depository Participants.
	
j.	
In line with the MCA Circular, the Notice calling 
the AGM has been uploaded on the website of the 
Company at http://infra-in.se.com. The Notice can 
also be accessed from the websites of the Stock 
Exchanges i.e. BSE Limited and National Stock 
Exchange of India Limited at www.bseindia.com and 
www.nseindia.com respectively and the AGM Notice 
is also available on the website of NSDL (agency 
for providing the Remote e-Voting facility) i.e. 
www.evoting.nsdl.com.
	
k.	
Since the AGM will be held through VC/OAVM, the 
Route Map and attendance slip is not annexed to this 
Notice.
	
l.	
Dispute Resolution: SEBI vide Master Circular 
No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-3/P/CIR/2023/195 
dated December 28, 2023, as updated from time 
to time, has established a common Online Dispute 
Resolution Portal (“ODR Portal”) for resolution of 
disputes arising in the Indian securities market. 
Pursuant to the above-mentioned circulars, after 
exhausting the option to resolve their grievances 
with the RTA / Company directly and through 
the existing SCORES platform, investors may 
initiate dispute resolution through the ODR Portal 
(https://smartodr.in/login), which can also be 
accessed through the Company’s website at 
https://infra-in.se.com/en/investor.jsp.
	
m.	
Recorded transcript of the meeting shall be uploaded 
on the website of the Company and the same shall 
also be maintained in safe custody of the Company.
3.	
PROCESS FOR THOSE MEMBERS WHOSE EMAIL IDs 
ARE NOT REGISTERED FOR PROCURING USER ID 
AND PASSWORD AND REGISTRATION OF EMAIL IDS 
FOR E-VOTING ON THE RESOLUTIONS SET OUT IN 
THIS NOTICE:
	
a.	
Those Members, who hold shares in physical form or 
who have not registered their email address with the 
Company and who wish to participate in the AGM or 
cast their vote through remote e-Voting or through 
the e-Voting system during the Meeting, may obtain 
the login ID and password by sending scanned copy 
of: i) a signed request letter mentioning name, folio 
number and complete address; and ii) self-attested 
scanned copy of the PAN Card and any document 
(such as Driving License, Bank Statement, Election 
Card, Passport, Aadhar Card) in support of the 
address of the Member as registered with the 
Company to the email address of the Company at 
company.secretary@schneider-electric.com or RTA 
at investor.helpdesk@in.mpms.mufg.com or to NSDL 
at evoting@nsdl.com.
	
b.	
In case shares are held in demat mode, Members may 
obtain the login ID and password by sending scanned 
copy of (i) a signed request letter mentioning name, 
DP ID-Client ID (16 digit DP ID + Client ID or 16 
digit beneficiary ID); (ii) self-attested scanned copy 
of client master or Consolidated Demat Account 
statement; and (iii) self-attested scanned copy of the 
PAN Card, to the email address of the Company at 
company.secretary@schneider-electric.com or RTA 
at investor.helpdesk@in.mpms.mufg.com or to NSDL 
at evoting@nsdl.com.
4.	
INSTRUCTIONS FOR E-VOTING DURING THE AGM 
ARE AS UNDER:
	
a.	
Upon declaration by the Chairperson about the 
commencement of e-Voting during the AGM, 
Members who have not cast their vote using remote 
e-Voting, shall do so by following the e-Voting 
instructions mentioned below for remote e-Voting.
	
b.	
Only those Members, who will be present in the AGM 
through VC/OAVM and have not cast their vote on 
the resolutions through remote e-Voting and are 
otherwise not barred from doing so, shall be eligible 
to vote through e-Voting system during the AGM.
	
c.	
The Members who have cast their vote by remote 
e-Voting prior to the AGM may also participate in the 
AGM through VC/ OAVM but shall not be entitled to 
cast their vote again.
	
d.	
The details of the person who may be contacted 
for any grievances connected with the facility for 
e-Voting on the day of the AGM shall be the same 
person mentioned for remote e-Voting.
5.	
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PARTICIPATING IN THE AGM 
THROUGH VC/OAVM ARE AS UNDER:
	
a.	
Members will be provided with a facility to attend 
the AGM through VC/OAVM platform provided by 
NSDL. Members may access the same by following 
the steps mentioned below for Access to NSDL 
e-Voting system. After successful login, you can see 
the link of VC/OAVM placed under “Join Meeting” 
menu against the Company name. You are requested 
to click on the VC/OAVM link placed under “Join 
Meeting” menu. The link for the AGM will be available 
in shareholder/member login where the EVENT of 
the Company will be displayed.
	
b.	
Please note that the Members who do not have 
User ID and Password for e-Voting or who have 
forgotten the User ID and Password may retrieve the 
same by following the remote e-Voting instructions 
mentioned in this Notice.
	
d.	
Members are encouraged to join the Meeting through 
Laptops for better experience.
	
e.	
Further, Members will be required to allow Camera, 
if any, and hence use internet with a good speed to 
avoid any disturbance during the Meeting.
	
f.	
While all efforts will be made to make the VC/ OAVM 
meeting smooth, Members connecting from mobile 
devices or tablets or through laptops etc. connecting 
via mobile hotspot, may experience Audio/ Video

loss due to fluctuation in their respective network. 
It is therefore recommended to use stable Wi-Fi or 
LAN connection to mitigate any kind of aforesaid 
glitches.
	
g.	
Registration as speaker shareholder: Members 
who would like to ask questions/ express their views 
during the AGM may register themselves as a speaker 
by sending their request from their registered 
e-mail ID mentioning their name, DP ID and Client 
ID/Folio number, PAN, mobile number at company.
secretary@schneider-electric.com. The Speaker 
Registration or the option for posting the questions 
shall be available from Monday, September 7, 2026 
(9 a.m. IST) till Wednesday, September 9, 2026 (5 
p.m. IST). The queries may be raised precisely and 
in brief to enable the Company to answer the same 
suitably depending on the availability of time at the 
Meeting. The Company reserves the right to restrict 
the number of speakers depending on the availability

Mr. Udai Singh was initially appointed as Managing Director 
& Chief Executive Officer of the Company for an initial period 
of three (3) years with effect from September 15, 2023. His 
current term is set to conclude on September 14, 2026 and 
consequently, he is now proposed to be re-appointed as 
Managing Director, designated as Managing Director & Chief 
Executive Officer (MD & CEO) of the Company for a further 
period of three (3) years.
During his tenure, Mr. Udai Singh has provided strong 
leadership and valuable strategic direction to the Company. 
Under his guidance, the Company has continued to progress 
and strengthen its position.
Brief profile of Mr. Udai Singh is as under:
"Mr. Udai Singh joined L&T in E&A as a Graduate Engineer 
Trainee (GET) in 1992 and over the last 33+ years of association 
with the organization, he has held various roles in the areas 
of Sales, Marketing, Projects & Contract management, and 
Manufacturing operations and his last role as Business Head 
for Equipment Business. Mr. Singh is a well-known professional 
in the industry, holding a bachelor’s degree in electrical 
engineering from IIT Varanasi and has undertaken various 
leadership programs at Ross Business school & INSEAD."
Taking into consideration the size and nature of the operations of 
the Company and keeping in mind Mr. Singh’s broad functional 
and general management skills, the NRC and Board believe 
that his continuation on the Board will be in the interest of the

At Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (‘Schneider 
Electric’, ‘SEIL’, ‘the Company’), we are advancing alongside 
India’s evolving energy ambitions, while supporting the nation’s 
transition towards a digitally enabled, sustainable economy. 
Through next-generation grid technologies and integrated 
solutions, we are helping shape resilient infrastructure, 
strengthen energy networks and accelerate industrial, 
technological and economic transformation. 
Our solutions help industries, utilities and communities 
manage energy with greater reliability, efficiency and agility 
amidst an increasingly complex operating environment. 
Leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced analytics, 
and digital innovation, we help customers modernise 
infrastructure, optimise performance and streamline decision-
making across the energy value chain.

protection relays, distribution management systems and 
next-generation smart grid solutions, including self-healing 
networks and E-Houses. These capabilities address diverse 
end markets such as power generation, transmission, 
distribution, oil and gas, metro rail, mining, metals and other 
infrastructure sectors, including electro-intensive industries.

bring together connected technologies, software, and 
services to improve system visibility, safety, operational 
continuity and sustainability outcomes in a dynamic and 
competitive landscape.

solutions that strengthen infrastructure resilience and 
support India’s growth journey.

prospects and competitive differentiation?

advanced solutions designed to support the growing 
demand for intelligent, connected, and sustainable 
energy infrastructure.

generation Trihal dry-type transformers, which combine high 
safety standards, operational reliability, and environmental 
performance, making them particularly well-suited for

Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited prioritises 
resilience as a key driver of sustainable growth and long-
term value creation. Our risk management approach 
is aligned with responsible business practices and 
is designed to help the Company operate efficiently 
within India’s evolving regulatory, economic and 
operational environment. 
Our Enterprise Risk Management framework is based on 
the three lines of defence model, ensuring structured 
oversight and clear accountability. 
Central functions define policies, frameworks and control 
mechanisms, while business units and functional teams 
own and manage risks by implementing these protocols 
within their respective operations.
This integrated approach enables consistent 
identification, assessment and mitigation of risks 
across the organisation. It strengthens operational 
stability, fortifies regulatory compliance and supports 
informed decision-making to address emerging risks and 
opportunities in the Indian market.

Strengthening  
Climate Resilience
Schneider Electric assesses both physical and transition 
risks associated with climate change. Physical risks 
include acute events such as floods, heatwaves, droughts, 
wildfires, storms and extreme cold, as well as chronic risks 
such as rising temperatures and water stress. These risks 
could disrupt operations, damage assets, increase cooling 
and water-related costs, and create supply-chain and 
logistics bottlenecks.
To manage these risks, the Group uses climate-risk modelling, 
site-level assessments, business continuity planning and 
regular audits. It conducts 60–80 audits annually and 
updates site risk profiles based on the findings. In response 
to the Group’s findings, SEIL has adopted measures like 
fire-protection systems, flood-response plans, employee 
preparedness training, HVAC upgrades, water recycling, 
supply-chain mapping, strategic inventory and dual sourcing. 
Critical manufacturing sites and logistics hubs are also 
reviewed to strengthen operational resilience.
Transition risks include regulatory, reputational and market-
related factors arising from climate policies, carbon pricing, 
evolving customer expectations and demand for low-
carbon products. Schneider Electric views decarbonisation, 
electrification, energy efficiency, automation and digital 
infrastructure as long-term growth drivers. Its response 
encompasses value-chain decarbonisation, delivery of its 
net-zero commitments, product eco-design, low-carbon 
solutions, responsible marketing, ESG screening and proactive 
regulatory compliance.

Advancing Water 
Stewardship
We recognise water as a critical shared resource and follow a 
proactive stewardship approach. Our manufacturing facilities 
in Vadodara are located in a water-stressed region, as identified 
by the World Resources Institute’s Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas. 
We have therefore embedded water management into our 
sustainability framework, with three key priorities:
•	 Reducing dependence on freshwater resources
•	 Maximising water reuse and recycling through 
circular systems
•	 Achieving zero or minimal discharge into the environment
All the sites have taken targets to implement water-related 
initiative and 100% of our sites have implemented all water-
related actions.
We have installed rainwater harvesting systems to capture 
monsoon runoff for secondary use and ensure the reuse 
of treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants for 
gardening. Water recycling plants and Zero Liquid Discharge 
systems further enable the treatment, recovery and reuse of 
water within our operations, reducing freshwater withdrawal 
and discharge. Last year, 30% water for the domestic purposes 
in MVI factory was met through rainwater harvesting.
Schneider Electric views circularity as a powerful lever 
for enabling a net-zero and nature-positive future. Its 
approach focuses on designing out waste and pollution, 
keeping products and materials in use for longer, and 
reducing dependence on virgin resources and energy-
intensive manufacturing.
Aligned with this ambition, we have ensured that all our 
sites are classified as 'Waste to Resource' sites, with >99% 
of non-hazardous waste diverted from landfill to recycling 
or energy recovery operation. Also, we have embedded the 
following features:
Design and Innovate: Applying eco-design principles 
to improve reliability, durability and product life, while 
exploring service-led business models.
Use Better: Increasing the use of sustainable and recycled 
materials while reducing manufacturing scrap and waste.
Use Longer: Extending product life through on-site repair, 
maintenance and equipment modernisation.
Use Again: Recirculating products, components and 
materials through take-back, refurbishment and resale of 
retired assets.
We recognise that the greatest value can be retained during 
the design and innovation stage, while recovery becomes 
increasingly resource-intensive later in the product lifecycle. 
For example, optimising copper use during manufacturing is 
more efficient than recovering it from end-of-life products.

Lifetime Extension through Ecofit Offers
In FY 2025-26, SEIL advanced its circularity and customer 
sustainability agenda by repairing and servicing circuit 
breakers through Schneider Electric’s EcoFit offers. This

modernisation and circularity services are designed to

avoid premature replacement by retrofitting, repairing or 
upgrading active components instead of replacing complete

reduces material consumption and lowers associated CO₂ 
emissions, while enabling customers to maintain continuity

maintenance costs. Through Ecofit solutions, we have 
refurbished more than 10,000 products on-site, delivering 
material and cost savings for customers while supporting a 
more circular and resource-efficient economy.
Embedding Circularity in Operations
We embed circularity across our value chain to minimise 
waste and optimise material utilisation. Through 
sustained prevention, reduction and recovery initiatives, 
we have achieved over 99% waste recovery, advancing 
our commitment to Zero Waste to Landfill and greater 
material circularity.
Packaging remains an important area of focus. We are 
transitioning to recyclable corrugated materials, reducing 
wood-based packaging, eliminating single-use plastics and 
adopting coconut coir as an alternative to plastic foam. We 
have also replaced wooden pallets with metal pallets under 
circular models and introduced reusable metal cages that can 
be used approximately 50 times.
These efforts are supported by segregation at source, 
recycling and recovery, as well as the conversion of organic 
waste into compost through vermicomposting and food-waste 
processing. Collaboration across procurement, manufacturing 
and logistics, together with supplier and partner engagement, 
helps us scale circular solutions across the value chain.
Eco-designing Sustainable Products
Design and innovation are central to our circularity 
approach. By embedding EcoDesign principles into product 
development, we seek to reduce material footprints, improve 
energy efficiency, extend product life and minimise end-of-
life impacts.
Our approach considers the complete product lifecycle, 
including materials, energy efficiency, durability, recirculation, 
packaging and operations. This enables us to develop 
products that use resources more efficiently, remain in service 
longer and can be reused, repaired, refurbished or recycled 
after their first life. Service-led business models further 
support customers in reducing CO₂ emissions and improving 
resource efficiency.
We align with Schneider Electric’s circularity ambition by 
placing design at the centre of our sustainable product and 
operations strategy. Our focus is on reducing dependence 
on virgin resources, improving product durability and 
repairability, and developing solutions that help customers

lifecycle assessments, environmental footprint measurement, 
repairability principles and the Environmental Data Program, 
provide a strong framework for advancing circularity across 
our value chain. By integrating these principles into offer 
creation, product design, manufacturing and customer 
solutions, we support the broader objective of decoupling 
business growth from natural resource extraction and 
advancing net-zero and nature-positive outcomes.

Growth Drivers 
The Indian economy continues to exhibit strong resilience and steady growth, with real GDP estimated to 
have grown by 7.7% in FY 2025-26, according to the Second Advance Estimates of the National Statistics 
Office. This sustained momentum reflects robust underlying economic fundamentals and positions 
India among the fastest-growing major economies globally. The outlook remains supported by rising 
productivity, broad-based development, and policy emphasis on inclusiveness and stability, reinforcing 
the country’s long-term trajectory towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
India’s power distribution segment remains a critical pillar of 
the electricity ecosystem, ensuring reliable delivery of power 
to consumers amid rising demand driven by industrial growth, 
urbanisation, and increasing electrification. Improving the 
operational efficiency and financial sustainability of DISCOMs 
continues to be a major policy priority, particularly given 
longstanding challenges such as high Aggregate Technical 
and Commercial (AT&C) losses, tariff revision delays, and 
the gap between Average Cost of Supply (ACS) and Average 
Revenue Realised (ARR).
To address these issues, the Revamped Distribution Sector 
Scheme (RDSS), with an outlay of `3.03 lakh crore from 
FY2021–22 to FY2025–26, has accelerated infrastructure 
modernisation, loss reduction, and billing efficiency 
improvements. Initiatives such as smart metering, feeder 
segregation, and deployment of SCADA, ADMS, and GIS 
technologies are enhancing operational visibility, grid 
reliability, and system control. The Draft National Electricity 
Policy (NEP) 2026 further reinforces the focus on smart 
grids, renewable integration, and higher-voltage distribution 
systems to strengthen network efficiency and capacity.
(Source: PIB)

India’s Clean Energy Transition
India’s energy transition is accelerating, supported by 
strong policy measures, ambitious targets, and sustained 
investments in clean energy infrastructure. The Government’s 
goal of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 
highlights the country’s shift towards a cleaner and more 
diversified energy mix. As of 31 March 2026, India’s installed 
renewable energy capacity stood at approximately 274.68 
GW, led by solar and wind power.
Strengthening grid infrastructure through initiatives such 
as the Green Energy Corridor remains critical for efficient 
renewable integration. At the same time, energy storage 
systems and digital grid technologies are becoming 
increasingly important for managing intermittency, improving 
flexibility, and enhancing system reliability. Beyond power 
generation, initiatives such as the National Green Hydrogen 
Mission are supporting industrial decarbonisation and 
the development of a broader clean energy ecosystem, 
accelerating India’s transition towards a low-carbon and 
resilient energy future.
(Source: PIB, MNRE)
India’s Infrastructure Sector
India’s infrastructure sector continues to play a pivotal 
role in driving economic growth, supported by strong 
policy measures, rising investments, and increasing 
private participation. Programmes such as PM Gati Shakti 
are accelerating integrated infrastructure development 
across transportation, logistics, power systems, and urban 
infrastructure, with a growing focus on sustainability, 
efficiency, and resilience.
The railway sector is witnessing significant transformation 
through electrification, network modernisation, and capacity 
expansion under the National Rail Plan 2030, which targets 
100% electrification and higher freight modal share. 
Expansion of Vande Bharat trains and metro rail networks is 
strengthening passenger mobility and supporting sustainable 
urban transportation. India's operational metro rail network 
expanded to more than 1,155 km across 26 cities in 2026, 
reinforcing the country's position as home to the world's third-
largest metro network and reflecting sustained investments in 
urban mass transit infrastructure.

including AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission, Swachh Bharat

Indian Mining, Metals and Minerals  
(MMM) Sector
India’s mining, metals, and minerals (MMM) sector remains 
a key pillar of the country’s industrial and infrastructure 
ecosystem, supplying critical raw materials for steel, 
cement, power, transportation, and construction. Rising 
infrastructure development and manufacturing activity 
continue to drive demand, supported by India’s diversified 
mineral base including coal, iron ore, bauxite, and limestone.
Policy reforms such as amendments to the MMDR Act and 
transparent auction processes have improved regulatory 
clarity and encouraged greater private participation. 
Increasing focus on critical minerals and rare earth 
elements through initiatives such as the National Critical 
Mineral Mission is supporting the development of domestic 
value chains for clean energy technologies, electric 
mobility, and advanced manufacturing. These efforts aim 
to strengthen supply security, reduce import dependence, 
and enhance India’s position in the global critical 
minerals ecosystem.
Simultaneously, adoption of automation, digital monitoring, 
advanced processing technologies, and electrified 
equipment is transforming mining operations by improving 
efficiency, safety, and resource utilisation. Supported by 
policy momentum, technology integration, and sustained 
industrial demand, the MMM sector is expected to 
remain a key driver of India’s long-term industrial and 
economic growth.
Indian Oil and Gas Sector
India’s oil and gas sector remains critical to economic 
growth and energy security, supporting demand from 
transportation, industry, aviation, and urbanisation. Petroleum 
products continue to form a key part of the energy mix, while 
natural gas is gaining importance as a transition fuel due 
to its relatively lower emissions. Continued investments in 
refining capacity, downstream infrastructure, and logistics 
are strengthening supply resilience and supporting India’s 
position as a major hub for refined petroleum products.
Natural gas is increasingly central to the energy transition, 
supported by expansion of pipeline networks, liquefied natural 
gas (LNG) infrastructure, and City Gas Distribution (CGD) 
systems aimed at improving accessibility and reliability. Policy 
reforms such as the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing 
Policy (HELP) and the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) 
are encouraging exploration, enhancing transparency and 
supporting long-term sector competitiveness. In parallel, the 
adoption of digital technologies, automation and advanced 
energy management systems is improving operational 
efficiency, optimising energy use and reducing environmental 
impact across the value chain.
Indian Mobility Sector
India’s mobility sector maintained strong momentum in 
FY 2025–26, supported by economic growth, infrastructure 
expansion, and rising consumption. The Indian automobile 
industry recorded its highest-ever annual domestic sales 
in FY 2025-26, with total vehicle wholesales reaching 
28.27 million units, up 10.4% year on year. All major vehicle 
segments, including passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, 
three-wheelers and two-wheelers, achieved record annual 
sales, reflecting broad-based growth across the industry.
Infrastructure development continued to play a critical 
role, with sustained investments in highways, expressways, 
and freight corridors improving connectivity and logistics 
efficiency across key economic regions.
Electrification is emerging as a structural trend, supported 
by government initiatives such as the Faster Adoption and 
Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (FAME) scheme and the 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, with strong growth 
in electric two- and three-wheelers. In parallel, the increasing 
adoption of digital technologies, including connected vehicles 
and telematics, is enhancing performance monitoring, 
enabling predictive maintenance, and improving overall 
operational efficiency.
Together, these trends are driving the evolution of India’s 
mobility ecosystem toward more efficient, technology-
enabled, and sustainable transportation solutions.

India’s Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure
India’s electric vehicle ecosystem expanded steadily in 
FY 2025–26, driven by policy support, rising investments, and 
growing consumer adoption. EV registrations crossed 2.45 
million units, reflecting ~24–25% year-on-year growth, with 
penetration increasing to ~8.5% from 7.7% in the previous 
year. Growth continued to be led by electric two- and three-
wheelers, while passenger EV adoption gained momentum.
Charging infrastructure also scaled up across urban centres, 
highways, and commercial hubs, supported by investments 
from utilities, oil marketing companies, and private operators. 
The rollout of fast charging, battery swapping, and smart 
charging solutions improved accessibility.
Adoption is expanding beyond metros into Tier 2 and Tier 
3 cities, aided by better infrastructure, wider product 
availability, and supportive state policies. Ongoing 
advancements in battery technology, charging networks and 
integration with renewable energy are expected to further 
accelerate India’s transition to sustainable mobility.
(Source: JMK)
India’s Battery Energy Storage System 
(BESS) Market
India’s Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) market is 
emerging as a key enabler of the country’s clean energy 
transition, supporting the rapid expansion of solar and 
wind capacity. As renewable generation increases, energy 
storage is becoming essential for managing intermittency, 
enhancing grid stability, and enabling reliable round-the-clock 
power supply.
During FY 2025-26, the BESS ecosystem gained further 
momentum, supported by favourable policy measures and a 
growing project pipeline. The Government of India’s Viability 
Gap Funding (VGF) scheme, with an outlay of `3,760 crore, 
aims to support the development of 13,200 MWh of storage 
capacity, improving project viability and encouraging private 
sector participation.
According to the National Electricity Plan, India’s energy 
storage requirement is projected to rise significantly from 
82.37 GWh in FY 2026-27 to 411.4 GWh by FY 2031-32. 
With declining battery costs, technological advancements, 
and increasing adoption across grid balancing, peak demand 
management and renewable integration, BESS is set to play 
a critical role in strengthening grid flexibility and supporting 
India’s long-term clean energy ambitions.
(Source: MNRE)
India’s Semiconductor Market 
India’s semiconductor market gained strong momentum 
in FY2025–26, driven by rising demand across consumer 
electronics, telecom, automotive electrification, data 
centres, and industrial automation. India is among the world's 
fastest-growing semiconductor markets, with domestic 
semiconductor demand projected to reach approximately 
USD 90 billion by FY2030, driven by rapid growth in 
electronics manufacturing, automotive electrification, data 
centres, AI and digital infrastructure. The Government is 
accelerating ecosystem development through the Semicon 
India Programme under the India Semiconductor Mission 
(ISM), backed by an incentive outlay of around USD 10 
billion. The initiative aims to strengthen capabilities across 
fabrication, ATMP, and chip design, while partnerships 
between global and domestic players are supporting 
the establishment of semiconductor manufacturing and 
packaging facilities. India’s strong semiconductor design 
talent base remains a significant advantage.
Supported by policy incentives, supply chain diversification, 
and rising investments, India is steadily emerging as a key 
hub for semiconductor design, manufacturing, and advanced 
electronics production.
(Source: NITI AAyog)

with the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) 
Rules, 2014, the Company has constituted an Environmental, 
Social and Governance and Corporate Social Responsibility 
Committee (“ESG & CSR Committee”) and adopted a CSR 
Policy outlining its approach towards the Company’s Corporate 
Social Responsibility initiatives.
The Company having reported profits in the previous financial 
year, was required to spend the prescribed amount towards 
Corporate Social Responsibility (“CSR”) activities for the 
financial year 2025-26. During the year under review, the 
Company undertook various CSR initiatives, inter alia, in the 
areas of skill development, community electrification across 
public health centers, Anganwadi centers and hospitals, and 
distribution of solar lamps in remote areas, thereby contributing 
to sustainable community development.
The Chief Financial Officer has certified that the funds 
earmarked for CSR related activities for financial year 2025-
26 have been utilized for the purpose and in the manner 
recommended by ESG & CSR Committee and approved by the 
Board of Directors.
The Board has also adopted an ESG Charter to integrate ESG 
considerations into the Company’s business strategy and to 
define its sustainability governance framework and long-term 
ambitions.
During the year, the composition of the ESG & CSR Committee 
was reconstituted with effect from October 24, 2025, and 
subsequently, on May 21, 2026, following the close of the 
financial year.
The ESG & CSR Committee met once during the year under 
review.
The Company has in place a CSR Policy, which is available 
on the website of the Company at https://download.se.com/
files?p_enDocType=Institutional+Document&p_Doc_Ref=CSR_
policy_2021.

disclosures are covered in the Annual Report on CSR activities,

Corporate Governance Report
Corporate governance is an integral ongoing commitment 
towards sustainable value creation for all stakeholders. It 
ensures that the affairs of the Company are conducted with 
integrity, transparency, and accountability, thereby fostering 
ethical, fair, and responsible business practices. A robust 
governance framework strengthens stakeholder confidence, 
including that of investors, employees, customers, and the 
broader community.
The Company’s governance philosophy is anchored in strong 
leadership and an effective Board of Directors ("Board"), 
which plays a critical role in guiding strategy, overseeing risk 
management, and ensuring compliance with applicable laws 
and regulatory requirements. This is supported by well-defined 
policies, robust internal control systems, and independent 
oversight mechanisms that promote disciplined and informed 
decision-making.
Transparency and accountability remain central to the 
Company’s governance practices. The Company endeavours to 
maintain clear and timely communication with stakeholders and 
ensures that management is accountable for its actions. This 
approach fosters a culture of responsibility, ethical conduct, and 
continuous improvement across all levels of the organization.
The Company believes that effective corporate governance 
is fundamental to its long-term sustainability, growth, and 
reputation. It enables prudent risk management, enhances 
operational efficiency, and supports informed strategic planning, 
thereby contributing to overall organizational resilience and 
performance.
This report is prepared in accordance with the provisions of 
the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“Listing 
Regulations”). In addition to complying with the requirements of 
Regulation 4(2) read with Chapter IV of the Listing Regulations, 
the Company continues to voluntarily adopt and adhere to the 
highest standards of corporate governance and ethical business 
conduct.
SCHNEIDER’S 
PHILOSOPHY 
ON 
CORPORATE 
GOVERNANCE
The world is transforming at an unprecedented speed and 
creating new opportunities and challenges that require agility, 
innovation and forward-looking leadership.
At Schneider Electric, we are committed to staying ahead of 
this transformation . As a global leader in energy technology, 
we electrify, automate, and digitalize industries, businesses, 
and homes - enabling greater efficiency, resilience, and 
sustainability.
Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (“the Company”), as a 
part of the Schneider Electric Group (“Schneider Electric” or the 
“Group”), follows a governance framework that is aligned with its 
values, business objectives, and stakeholder expectations. The 
Board of Directors continuously evaluates and strengthens the 
governance structure to ensure its effectiveness and relevance 
in a dynamic business environment. The governance model is 
designed to support the Company’s financial and sustainability 
performance, safeguard stakeholder interests, uphold 
shareholders' rights, and maintain an appropriate balance of 
authority and accountability across governance bodies.
The accelerating transition towards electrification, automation 
and digitalization continues to reshape the markets in which the 
Company operates. By advancing Energy Technology through 
Innovation and intelligent solutions, the Company seeks to 
create smarter, more efficient, and more resilient & sustainable 
systems. Our focus on technology leadership, customer 
differentiation, operational excellence, and responsible growth 
enables us to deliver sustainable growth and long-term value 
to all stakeholders.
The Company has established a robust corporate governance 
framework that places equal emphasis on performance, 
compliance, risk management, sustainability, and ethical 
business conduct. The framework is guided by the principles of 
integrity, transparency, accountability, fairness, and stakeholder 
inclusiveness, which form the foundation of all business 
decisions and actions.
Operating in a highly technical and safety-sensitive industry, the 
Company is committed to maintaining the highest standards 
of quality, environmental stewardship, health and safety, and 
regulatory compliance. Strong internal controls, effective 
risk management processes, and a culture of continuous 
improvement support innovation, operational excellence, 
and organizational resilience. The Company also promotes 
ethical decision-making at all levels and remains committed to 
sustainable growth, energy efficiency, and the development of 
reliable power solutions. By integrating responsible business 
practices with its strategic objectives, the Company continues 
to strengthen stakeholder trust and create enduring value for 
all its stakeholders.
TRUST CHARTER, SCHNEIDER ELECTRIC'S CODE OF 
CONDUCT
Schneider Electric developed the Trust Charter, with the 
support of various internal teams including Governance, 
Customer Satisfaction & Quality, Sustainability, Global Human 
Resources, Global Supply Chain, Global Finance, Global 
Marketing, and Corporate Citizenship. This document is made 
available to stakeholders through Schneider Electric’s website 
and is referenced within contractual relationships.
Schneider Electric believes that trust is a foundational value. It is 
earned. It serves as a compass, showing the true north in an ever 
more complex world, and the Group considers it to be core to 
its environment, sustainability, and governance commitments.
The Trust powers all Schneider Electric interactions with 
stakeholders and all relationships with customers, shareholders, 
employees, and the communities Schneider Electric serves, in 
a meaningful, inclusive, and positive way.

All Schneider Electric employees are expected to comply 
with Schneider Electric’s Trust programs. They are based on 
management commitment which makes its pillars effective and 
on risk assessment which assists decision making, determining 
the risks to be treated and the priority to implement the 
treatment.
Through its Trust programs, Schneider Electric aims to prevent, 
detect, and mitigate integrity risks including corruption, fraud, 
violation of human rights, health and safety, responsible 
workplace (including discrimination, harassment, and sexual 
harassment), anti-competitive practices, sanctions and export 
control, tax law, quality, cybersecurity, as well as data privacy and 
protection. The program design and operation are influenced 
by the Group’s risk profile, business model, organizational 
structure, and culture.
Each section of the Trust Charter states clear Do’s and 
Don’ts and provides clear references to relevant policies and 
procedures, which are adapted to meet local legal requirements 
when necessary. This Code of Conduct applies to everyone 
working at Schneider Electric or any of Schneider Electric’s 
subsidiaries. It is both an individual and collective responsibility 
to comply and respect laws and regulations, to apply Schneider 
Electric policies, and to uphold strong ethical principles to earn 
trust at all times.
Compliance by Board of Directors and Employees
The Company has adopted the Schneider Electric Trust 
Charter, which is applicable to all Directors, Senior Management 
Personnel, and employees of the Company. The Charter is 
available on the website of the Company for reference. It serves 
as the Company’s Code of Conduct ("Code") for its Directors, 
Senior Management Personnel and employees, laying down 
clear standards of ethical conduct, outlining specific do’s 
and don’ts, and provides references to relevant policies and 
procedures.
The Code has been duly circulated to all members of the Board 
and Senior Management Personnel. All such individuals have 
affirmed their compliance with the Code for the financial year 
ended March 31, 2026. A declaration to this effect, duly signed 
by the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer (CEO), forms 
part of this Report as Annexure A.
ANTI-CORRUPTION
At Schneider Electric, integrity is a non - negotiable standard. 
Acting ethically and responsibly is essential to earning trust and 
to building a sustainable, highperforming company.
The Company applies a zero-tolerance approach to corruption, 
bribery, and any form of unethical conduct, wherever it occurs. All 
managers must lead by example and actively promote a culture 
of integrity. All employees exposed to a higher corruption risk 
must complete mandatory anti-corruption training at least once 
a year as defined by Group Compliance. Any employee facing 
a doubtful situation must immediately consult their manager 
or the Compliance Department before acting. Disciplinary 
measures apply consistently at all levels of the organization, 
including management, and failure to prevent or escalate known 
risks may itself result in sanctions. In case of serious doubt about 
the behaviour of a third party or an employee which may be 
potentially contrary to the provisions of the policy, it sets out 
the process to report the concerns through the whistleblowing 
system.
A set of additional policies and procedures related to Conflict of 
Interest, Business Agents, Gifts & Hospitality, has been created 
to operationalize the behaviour rules of the Anti-Corruption 
policy.
The Anti-Corruption Policy considers the results of the risk 
assessment conducted with key internal stakeholders across 
all Group processes, as well as benchmarking actions to 
understand the expectations of external stakeholders, ensuring 
it is appropriately aligned. This policy acts as a handbook for 
all Schneider Electric employees and affiliates to be consulted 
when in doubt about the appropriate behaviour to adopt. It is 
not intended to address every issue one may encounter, but it 
provides appropriate examples of corruption risks and offers 
guidance to resolve many ethical dilemmas.
BOARD OF DIRECTORS
The Board of Directors of the Company comprises an optimum 
blend of Executive, Non-Executive and Independent including 
Woman Director, ensuring a balanced and effective governance 
structure. As on March 31, 2026, Independent Directors 
constitute 50% of the Board, reflecting the Company's 
commitment to strong governance, objective oversight, and 
independent judgment. The Board also seeks to maintain 
diversity across skills, experience, industry expertise, age, and 
professional backgrounds, thereby enabling well-informed and 
balanced decision-making.
Mr. Pravin Kumar Purang serves as the Chairperson of the Board 
and was appointed to this position by the Board of Directors 
with effect from November 6, 2025. Under his leadership, the 
Board continues to provide strategic guidance, promote high 
standards of corporate governance, and safeguard the long-
term interests of the Company's stakeholders.

Separate Independent Directors’ Meetings
Regulation 25 of the Listing Regulations and Schedule IV of 
the Act, read with the Rules thereunder mandates that the 
Independent Directors of the Company shall hold at least 
one meeting in a financial year, without the presence of Non- 
Independent Directors and executive Management.
At such meeting, the Independent Directors discuss, among 
other matters, the performance of the Company and risks faced 
by it, the flow of information to the Board, strategy, governance, 
compliance, Board movements, human resource matters and 
performance review of the Non-Independent Directors, the 
Board as a whole, including the Chairperson, and Executive 
Director(s).
Additionally, the Independent Directors also met separately with 
the Statutory and Internal Auditor to discuss key accounting 
issues, risks, overall control environment and to invite their 
overall feedback.
The Board is updated by the Independent Directors about the 
outcome of the meetings and actions, if any, required to be taken 
by the Company’s management.

SUCCESSION PLANNING
Succession plans in your Company correspond to a systematic, structured process for identifying and preparing employees with 
potential to fill key organizational positions, should the position become vacant. This process applies to all key positions including 
the Board of Directors and Key Managerial Personnels and SMP positions.
Succession plans are necessary processes to reduce risk of vacant positions or skill gap transitions, create a pipeline of future 
leaders, ensure full business continuity, and improve employee motivation and engagement.
The NRC aims at preparing for the future of the Company’s executive bodies, in particular through the establishment of a succession 
plan for executive officers. The plan, which is reviewed at meetings of the NRC, addressing various scenarios, such as:
•	
Unplanned vacancy due to prohibition, resignation, or death; and
•	
Planned vacancy due to retirement or expiration of term of office.
NRC reviews succession planning for Board, KMP and Senior Management positions, as considered appropriate, and makes 
recommendations to the Board from time to time.
Appointment process for Directors & KMPs
The selection process for Directors and KMPs is led by the NRC. When one or more directorships become vacant, or more broadly 
when the Board of Directors wishes to expand or modify its composition, the NRC documents and ranks the selection criteria for 
potential candidates, taking into account the desired balance and diversity in the Board’s composition. The Committee takes into 
account the diversity policy and the objectives defined by the Board of Directors in terms of skill set. Based on these criteria, the 
Committee steers the search for and selection of new Directors, where appropriate with the assistance of an external consultant, 
and conducts the necessary verifications. The members of the NRC then interview the candidates and issue a recommendation 
to the Board of Directors. The NRC focused on bringing to the Board an executive with experience as chair or a long tenure as a 
member of a Board or committee overseeing compensation, or with a technology or industry background.
Your Company believes that effective Board blends diverse perspectives with robust oversight. This involves leveraging the 
extensive experience of long-serving Directors who have a deep understanding of our business over several years, with the fresh 
insights of newer appointees. We aim for our Board composition to mirror the global nature of our business.

BOARD COMMITTEES
The Board has constituted various sub-committees with the 
primary objective of maintaining strong business fundamentals 
and delivering high performance through relentless focus on 
significant affairs of the Company.
Each committee is set up by the formal approval of the Board 
and is guided by its respective charter which clearly defines 
their purpose, roles and responsibilities.
The Board provides and evaluates the Company’s strategic 
direction, management policies and their effectiveness, and 
ensures that shareholders’ long-term interests are being 
served. The Board has constituted six Committees, viz. Audit 
Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, 
Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee, Environmental, Social

Procedure for Postal Ballot
The Postal Ballot process was conducted in compliance with the provisions of Sections 108 and 110 of the Companies Act, 2013 
(“the Act”), read with the rules made thereunder and applicable circulars issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”). The 
Company provided electronic voting (“e-voting”) facility to its Members and, for this purpose, engaged the services of National 
Securities Depository Limited (“NSDL”).
In view of the relaxations granted under the MCA circulars, the Postal Ballot Notice was sent only in electronic mode to those 
Members whose email addresses were registered with the Company/Registrar and Transfer Agent (“RTA”) or their Depository 
Participants as on the respective cut-off dates. The process of voting was conducted exclusively through remote e-voting. Further, 
the Company published the requisite advertisements in the newspapers, in compliance with the provisions of the Act and applicable 
rules and circulars.

For SEIL, sustainability is foundational to how we create long-term value. It 
informs the way we design and manufacture advanced products and systems 
for electricity distribution, how we operate our facilities, how we engage with 
suppliers and customers, and how we contribute to the communities around 
our sites. SEIL’s portfolio spanning transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, 
protection relays, automation systems, distribution management systems places 
us at the centre of India’s energy transition and the digital transformation of 
power infrastructure.

of SEIL’s commitment to responsible business, sustainability and governance 
excellence. We were also proud that Schneider Electric was ranked among India’s 
Top 15 Employers for 2025 by TIME and Statista, reflecting the strength of our 
people-first culture, inclusion agenda and commitment to employee experience. 
These efforts and recognitions has helped us to maintain “Strong” ESG rating by 
CRISIL, an independent ESG rating provider approved by SEBI.
Our sustainability strategy for FY 2025–26 continues to be anchored on the 
five long-term pillars of Climate, Resources, Trust, Equal and Generations. These 
priorities are aligned with Schneider Electric’s global sustainability framework 
and its SBTi-validated commitment to achieve a 25% absolute reduction in 
value-chain emissions by 2030 and net-zero CO₂ emissions across the value 
chain by 2050.

Accessibility of workplaces: Are the premises / 
offices of the entity accessible to differently abled 
employees and workers, as per the requirements 
of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 
2016? If not, whether any steps are being taken 
by the entity in this regard.
Yes. Our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI) Charter ensures 
that all SEIL workplaces are accessible and follow Local 
Government regulations. In 2025-26, we have enhanced 
our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policy and 
have also drafted a separate EEO policy for PwD calling 
out the accessibility support and support extended from 
organization's end to ensure disability inclusion. We have 
further strengthened our commitment to accessibility and 
inclusion for Persons with Disabilities (PwD) by curating 
an in-house comprehensive checklist. This checklist 
encompasses 21 critical touchpoints, ranging from site 
entrances to emergency exits, amounting to a total of 
200 checkpoints. We have prioritized sites based on the 
presence of PwD employees, self-declared through our 
"Count Me In" our voluntary campaign to share disability on 
the portal, and strategic sites with high headcount.
Our focus also extends to upcoming sites to ensure they 
meet accessibility standards from the outset. A thorough 
gap study has been conducted for all prioritized sites, 
and we are ready to implement the necessary changes. 
Following the revamp, most of our workforce will have 
access to fully accessible infrastructure. We continue to 
work with facility team, liaison officer, HR, and relevant 
stakeholders in ensuring accessible infrastructure for 
everyone.
Schneider Electric is dedicated to the inclusion of people 
with disabilities by raising awareness and breaking 
stereotypes, both internally and externally. Through 
our SAKSHAM program, we have made significant

10.	 Health and safety management system:
	
a.	
Whether an occupational health and safety 
management system has been implemented by 
the entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such 
system?
Yes. All sites/locations of SEIL have a robust 
occupational health and safety management system 
which is aligned with ISO 45001 – Occupational 
health and safety management system and 
are regularly audited by external auditors from 
accredited organizations. Internally, SEIL is driving 
OHS Management system through Safety & 
Environment Strategy which cover various pillars like 
“Technical qualification & self-behaviours”, “Leading 
as a role model”, “Operational discipline & execution” 
& “Safe workplace for everyone”. These pillars have 
five guiding principles and top five hazards. These 
top 5 hazards are derived from the proactive and 
reactive indicators which covers driving, falls, 
machines, electrical and powered industrial trucks. 
These hazards are addressed with the principles 
which are “Unsafe-We stop the work”, “We are 
qualified”, “We report opportunities”, “We resolve & 
share solutions” and “We care for each other”. The 
OH&S management system is assessed through EHS 
Assessment tool every year by internal auditors. EHS 
Assessment covers plant hazard profile, specific 
hazards mapping, 16 dedicated safety assessment

5.	
Details on assessment of value chain partners
To understand which of our supply chain partners are at 
higher risk of not meeting legal and international standards 
for Health, Safety & working conditions, SEIL leverages our 
partnership with Responsible Business Alliance (RBA), 
joined by Elevate, an ESG risk analysis company to annually 
analyze our direct & indirect suppliers across the world. 
The assessment marks each supplier on a scale of 10 (1 
being the lowest score and 10 being the highest score). 
If a supplier receives a score equal to or less than 5 then 
they are classified as a high-risk supplier and need to be 
assessed onsite as per the RBA standard. If a supplier 
receives a score equal to or lower than 7.5 and higher than 
5 then they are classified as medium risk and are provided 
with a remote questionnaire which covers core areas of 
the RBA audit.

remote questionnaire then an on-site audit is triggered.

devises a plan based on the available resources at the 
supplier site and implements it over time through multiple 
training and monitoring sessions with the supplier team.

team time to acclimate to the system and conducts an 
assessment after 3-6 months to review the effectiveness 
of the action plan.

to ensure long-term implementation.

transitioning to cleaner alternatives.

gas with electrification processes.

energy audits, digitalization, and optimization 
techniques to enhance efficiency.

RE100 and ongoing phase-wise installation of solar 
power, with the entity generating 20% of its power 
from solar.

Electric Vehicle Adoption: Promoting green mobility 
through the installation of EV charging stations for 
employees.

robust filling procedures, advanced leakage

in CO2 generation.

leakages, installing occupancy sensors in offices, 
insulating HVAC chiller pumps and optimizing their 
usage, and implementing operational controls during 
non-occupancy hours.
8.

canteen's water heating.

System Segregation & Insulation: Segregating 
air-conditioned and kitchen exhaust systems and

SEIL maintains a comprehensive waste management 
program across all locations, monitoring waste generated 
from production, logistics, and office activities. Adhering 
to legal requirements, all hazardous waste is appropriately 
managed. A strong emphasis is placed on the 3 Rs (Reduce, 
Reuse, Recycle) for non-hazardous waste, with a target of 99% 
diversion from landfill. Special category wastes are recycled 
through Pollution Control Board-authorized vendors, and 
hazardous waste is treated via incineration or recycling. SEIL 
is actively driving towards a zero-landfill principle, ensuring 
no residues are sent to landfills.
1.

removing multiple bins to enhance proper separation 
of waste at the source.
2.

waste storage in scrap yards.
3.

before waste is dispatched for recycling to designated 
facilities.
4.

Employing recyclable wooden pallets, reusing carton 
boxes, transitioning to multi-use plastic containers 
for transport and storage, and optimizing packaging 
designs.
5.	
Eliminating Single-Use Plastics & Packaging 
Waste: Replacing plastic water bottles with steel 
alternatives, using compostable plastic bags in 
bins, adopting reusable metal boxes for busway line 
materials, redesigning wooden pallets for reduced 
wood consumption, giving packaging boxes a second 
life through internal reuse, implementing honeycomb 
and corrugated packaging as alternatives to wood, 
and utilizing returnable metal trolleys to eliminate 
packaging.
6.	
Metal Frame Implementation: Replacing wooden 
pallets with metal frame bases for incoming raw 
materials from vendors.
7.	
E-waste Recycling: Ensuring electronic waste is 
recycled through authorized vendors in compliance

the actions, roles, and responsibilities within the site to 
ensure the management of the initial phase following an

critical activities. It is focused on industrial activities.

supplier on a scale of 10 (1 being the lowest score and 10

responses to the remote questionnaire then an on-site 
audit is triggered

Revenue Recognition
Revenue from contracts with customers is recognized 
when control of the goods or services are transferred to 
the customer at an amount that reflects the consideration 
to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange 
for those goods or services.
The Company has concluded that as principal, it typically 
controls the goods or services before transferring them 
to the customers. There is an inherent risk and presumed 
fraud risk around the accuracy and existence of revenue 
recognised. Further, revenue is an important element 
of how the Company measures its performance. The 
Company focuses on revenue as a key performance 
measure, which could create an incentive for revenue to 
be recognized before the controls have been transferred.
Accordingly, due to the significant risk associated with 
revenue recognition in accordance with terms of Ind AS 
115 ‘Revenue from contracts with customers’, it has been 
determined a key audit matter in our audit of the financial 
statements.
In view of the above and given the Company and its 
stakeholders focus on revenue as a key performance 
indicator, we determined this to be a key audit matter.
In view of the significance of the matter, following audit 
procedures were applied in this area, amongst others to obtain 
sufficient and appropriate audit evidence:
 We assessed the appropriateness of the revenue recognition 
accounting policies and its compliance in terms of Ind AS 
115 ‘Revenue from contracts with customers’.
 We obtained an understanding of management’s internal 
controls over the revenue recognition process and evaluated 
the design and tested the operating effectiveness of key 
controls.
 We carried out analytical procedures on revenue recognised 
during the year to identify unusual variances and discussed 
with designated management personnel.
 We performed substantive procedures by testing the 
underlying documents on samples selected based on a 
representative sampling of revenue transactions recorded 
during the year.
 We performed cut-off testing on sales transactions made 
near the year-end on sample basis by obtaining supporting 
documentation including customer confirmation of receipt 
of goods to establish that sales and corresponding trade 
receivables are properly recorded in the correct period.
We tested the relevant disclosures made in the financial 
statements.
